Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph OPINION ND. _GI_ S. 2622 SEP 26 Mr. NELSON M. MOI-OD Adviser, Senior Citizen Organization San Narciso, Quezon Dear Mr. Molod: This refers to your letter dated May 17, 2023, requesting this Department's legal interpretation of the One Percent (1%) of the Senior Citizens/PWD (Persons with Disabilities) from the [National Tax Allotment] of the Barangay. Specifically, the issue hinges on the legal interpretation of the words "senior citizens" and "PWD" , punctuated by a slash vis-å-vis the 1% allocation. Foremost, it is to be noted that, as it stands, there is no national law that specifically mandates the local government units (LGUs) to allocate a certain portion of their respective National Tax Allotment—previously called the Internal Revenue Allotment— for senior citizens and PWDs. While there has been a proposed legislative measurel that seeks to mandate LGUs to allocate 1% of their NTA specifically for programs and projects for senior citizens and 1% for programs and projects for PWDs, the same has not been enacted into law as of yet. Being a proposed legislative measure, the same cannot be implemented yet, let alone used as the basis for the allocation Notwithstanding, the Department submits that there is no legal impediment for LGUs to allocate certain portions of their NTA to senior citizens and PWDs in pursuance of the general welfare and well-being of these sectors. We now delve into the instant query. This Department recognizes the ambiguity of how the phrase "senior citizens/PWD" punctuated by a slash (I) is framed. The same connotes synonyms. senior citizens and PWDs are two distinct sectors; hence, both terms should not be used interchangeably Linguistically speaking, however, the punctuation slash is also used to represent the word "or" or "and/or" to denote alternative or inclusivity. In this context, the phrase "senior citizens/PWD" is to be construed to mean that both sectors are entitled to 1% of the barangay N T A. As to the utilization or the manner by House Bill 2023 "Mandating Local Government units to Allocate One Percent (1 Of their Internal Revenue Allotment (IRA) for Programs and Projects for Senior Citlzens and 1 % Of IRA for Programs and Projects for Persons with Disabllities• Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline 8876-34-54

which the 1% allocation is divided to these sectors, eg whether it is to be divided equally or proportionately, the same is best determined by the concerned barangay Along this line, it is to be emphasized that Section 285 of the Local Government Code does not expressly define how LGUs should utilize their NTA share. There is no provision in the Local Government Code that we can find that dictates how LGUs should utilize their NTA share, save for the twenty percent (20%) Local Development Funds, lest it violate the principle of local and fiscal autonomy vested in LGUs. Lastly, it is equally important to emphasize that, in the exercise of their local fiscal autonomy, LGUs are mandated to endeavor to have a balanced budget—this is one of the fundamental principles underpinning local fiscal administration. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, Authority of the Secretary: ICTOR R. LLAMAS dersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affair OUSELLA/JVL,'LLLS-LRAL1.D/jam ARIEL O. IGLESIA, CESO Ill Regional Director.
